text:
sara: Heads-up — observed a regression on master for seq_len=1024 on A100s. Kernel selector picked the 'wide-tile' path and end-to-end throughput is down ~18% compared to the previous stable.

mike: I profiled a few runs with nsight/nvprof. Toplines: occupancy ~42%, shared mem utilization ~90%, register usage per thread ~92 -> spilling seen. NVTX slice shows kernel_take ~dominant. Snippet: 

```
== PROFBLOCK ==
Kernel: wide_tile_conv  Elapsed: 5.12ms  regs:92  sm_efficiency:42%
L1/shared: 18.3KB/64KB  achieved 89% of peak shared
LocalMem (spills): 1.2MB
Warp execution efficiency: 87%
```

mike: Also fusing the masked-softmax variant increased live regs; might be the main driver for the spill/regression.

jia: My mental model: the wide-tile kernel was tuned for V100 occupancy patterns (tile 64x64 mapping). On Ampere the warp/smem balance favors narrower per-warp tiles and more shared-memory tiling per CTA. Quick microbench on a copy of the kernel:

```
config A: tile=64x64  -> 6.2ms
config B: tile=128x32 -> 4.7ms
config C: tile=256x16 -> 5.0ms
```

jia: So 128x32 looks better for these seq_len shapes. Also try warp-specialization: have a variant where we launch 1 warp per microtile vs 4 warps per tile; that cuts L1 contention.

alex: Right — two things collide here: (1) the static kernel selector switches path at seq_len >= 512 -> picks wide-tile which used to be fine, (2) with fused ops register pressure crosses a threshold and the wide-tile variant spills. For certain batch sizes (batch<=8) the narrow-tile variant is actually faster even though the selector chooses wide.

alex: Proposal: add a small runtime autotune step on model load (or first warm invocation). Sample candidate kernels across representative (seq_len, batch) grid: seq_len in {64,256,1024}, batch in {1,4,8,16}. For each cell run N iterations and record median throughput + p95 latency, then build a table for the selector to consult. Fallback rule: prefer kernel with lowest median latency, but also reject any candidate with p95 > 1.2x baseline. Example config: 

```json
{"autotune": true, "candidates": ["narrow_tile","wide_tile","128x32_specialized"], "sample_grid": [[64,1],[256,4],[1024,8]], "shots": 8}
```

sara: That sounds reasonable. Can we make autotune async and cached per model+quantization so it doesn't add cold-start for the first real traffic? Also add a canary-only rollout for Dedicated and Private first.

mike: Small note — splitting fused softmax+mask into two kernels reduced regs from 92 -> 74 in my bench and removed spills, improving throughput ~12% for the wide-tile path. Might be an easy immediate win while we iterate on tile sizes.

perf-bot: canary run @1750001500: new autotune + 128x32 specialization enabled on a 4-GPU dedicated pool. Results: seq_len=1024 batch=8 throughput +6%, p99 latency reduced 9% on average, but one machine showed p99 increase ~22% (investigating). :eyes:

sara: Good — please open tracking issue INV-3422 with the failing host trace. Put autotune disabled by default until we have more canary data. For next steps: (1) mike to land split-softmax patch (2) jia to push 128x32 kernel variant and microbench harness (3) alex to prototype the device-side autotune state table and cache. I'll schedule a quick sync tomorrow to review canary traces. :thumbsup:

mike: ack, will PR split-softmax today.

jia: I'll drop perf numbers into INV-3422 once I push microbench results.

alex: I'll sketch selector changes and a small guard to fallback if latency >1.2x baseline.

sara: Thanks all — moving to tracking.
